items.title: Section: Fascicle Thirty-Nine Opens — The Six Perfections That Complete Buddhahood

items.zh: 復次，菩薩次第圓滿六波羅蜜多已，能證無上正等菩提。謂施波羅蜜多、戒波羅蜜多、忍波羅蜜多、精進波羅蜜多、靜慮波羅蜜多、慧波羅蜜多。
items.en: Furthermore, once bodhisattvas have, in due order, brought the six perfections to completion, they are able to realise unsurpassed, perfect awakening. These are: the perfection of giving, the perfection of discipline, the perfection of patience, the perfection of diligence, the perfection of meditative concentration, and the perfection of wisdom.

items.title: Section: The Perfection of Giving Opens — Worldly Giving, and Giving That Truly Crosses to the Far Shore

items.zh: 云何菩薩施波羅蜜多？
items.en: What is a bodhisattva's perfection of giving?

items.title: Section: Nine Aspects of Giving, in a Verse Worth Memorising

items.zh: 嗢拕南曰：自性、一切、難、一切門、善士、一切種、遂求、二世樂、清淨，如是九種相，是名略說施。
items.en: The summarising verse states: intrinsic nature, comprehensiveness, difficulty, universal scope, purity of motive, completeness across every circumstance, responsiveness to what is asked for, benefit in both this life and the next, and freedom from taint — these nine aspects are, in brief, called giving.

items.zh: 謂九種相施，名為菩薩施波羅蜜多。一、自性施，二、一切施，三、難行施，四、一切門施，五、善士施，六、一切種施，七、遂求施，八、此世他世樂施，九、清淨施。
items.en: These nine aspects of giving are called a bodhisattva's perfection of giving: first, giving in its intrinsic nature; second, comprehensive giving; third, difficult giving; fourth, giving through every gateway; fifth, giving by a genuinely good person; sixth, giving complete in every kind; seventh, giving that fulfils what is asked; eighth, giving that brings joy in this life and the next; ninth, pure giving.

items.title: Section: The Intrinsic Nature of Giving — Not Every Gift Should Be Given

items.zh: 云何菩薩自性施？謂諸菩薩於自身財無所顧惜，能施一切所應施物。無貪俱生思，及因此所發能施一切無罪施物身語二業，安住律儀阿笈摩見、定有果見，隨所希求，即以此物而行惠施。當
items.en: What is a bodhisattva's giving in its intrinsic nature? Bodhisattvas, having no attachment to their own body or wealth, are able to give away whatever should genuinely be given. This consists of the volition accompanied by non-greed, and the deeds of body and speech this volition gives rise to, able to give whatever blameless object is called for; resting in moral discipline, correct view of the teaching, and certainty that giving bears fruit; and, according to whatever is genuinely sought, giving that very thing.

items.title: Section: Certainty That Giving Bears Fruit — Four Classical Patterns of Giving and Reward

items.zh: 知是名菩薩自性施。
items.en: Certainty that giving bears fruit means holding a settled, confident understanding of cause and effect, knowing that giving must yield its result, and giving not because led by some outside influence, but from one's own genuine conviction.

items.title: Section: Comprehensive Giving Opens — What Counts as "Everything" Given

items.zh: 云何菩薩一切施？謂一切者略有二種。一、內所施物，二、外所施物。若諸菩薩但捨己身，是名唯施內所施物。
items.en: What is a bodhisattva's comprehensive giving? "Everything," in brief, is of two kinds: first, what is given from within; second, what is given from without. If bodhisattvas give only their own body, this is called giving only what is given from within.

items.zh: 若諸菩薩為愍食吐活命眾生，數數食已，吐所飲食而施與之，是名雜施內外施物。若諸菩薩除上所說，施餘一切所應施物，是名唯施外所施物。
items.en: If bodhisattvas, out of compassion for a being that lives on food it cannot chew, repeatedly eat and then bring up that food to feed it, this is called mixed giving of both what is given from within and from without. If bodhisattvas, apart from what has been described above, give every other object that should genuinely be given, this is called giving only what is given from without.

items.zh: 又諸菩薩略由二相，以自內身施來求者。

items.title: Section: Giving One's Own Body — Total Surrender, and Piece by Piece

items.zh: 一、總求身者，以身施彼，隨所欲為，繫屬於彼、隨順於彼。譬如有人為衣食故，強自為他而作僕使。如是菩薩無愛染心，但為速證最勝菩提，但為眾生利益安樂，但為布施波羅蜜多速圓滿故，以身施彼，隨所欲為，繫屬於彼、隨順於彼。
items.en: First, for one who requests the entire body: giving the body to that person, to do with as they wish, belonging entirely to them, following their will entirely. Just as someone, for the sake of food and clothing, forces themselves to serve another as a servant — so too a bodhisattva, with no craving mind at all, but only in order to swiftly realise supreme awakening, only for beings' benefit and happiness, only to swiftly perfect the perfection of giving, gives the body to that person, to do with as they wish, belonging entirely to them, following their will entirely.

items.zh: 二、別求手、足、頭、目、支節、血、肉、筋、骨乃至髓者，隨其所欲，一切施與。
items.en: Second, for one who specifically requests hands, feet, head, eyes, limbs, blood, flesh, sinew, bone, or even marrow: giving all of it, according to what they wish.

items.zh: 又諸菩薩亦由二相，以外施物施諸眾生。

items.title: Section: Giving External Things — What's Requested for Use, and Full Transfer of Ownership

items.zh: 一、求受用者，恣彼所須，如其所樂隨意受用。
items.en: First, for one who seeks something to use: freely providing whatever they lack, letting them use it as they please, entirely according to their own preference.

items.zh: 二、求自在者，一切斷心並皆施與。
items.en: Second, for one who seeks genuine ownership: giving it entirely, with a mind that lets go completely. ... Being able to do with it entirely as one wishes is what "ownership" means here. If that being, through receiving this gift, does not thereby fall into arrogance or unwholesome conduct, and does not thereby strengthen any unwholesome root, this is called a mind that lets go completely.

items.title: Section: Wise Giving — Sometimes Planting a Seed First, Sometimes Withholding Entirely

items.zh: 又諸菩薩非無差別以一切種一切內外所有施物施諸眾生；是諸菩薩以其種種內外施物，於諸眾生或有施與、或不施與。云何施與？云何不施？
items.en: Bodhisattvas do not, without any discernment, give every kind of internal and external object to every being; rather, with their various internal and external gifts, bodhisattvas sometimes give and sometimes do not give. What determines giving? What determines not giving?

items.zh: 謂諸菩薩，若知種種內外施物，於彼眾生唯令安樂、不作利益；或復於彼不作安樂、不作利益，便不施與。若知種種內外施物，於彼眾生定作利益、不定安樂，或復於彼定作利益、定作安樂，即便施與。
items.en: Bodhisattvas, if they know that some internal or external gift would bring a being only pleasure without benefit, or would bring neither pleasure nor benefit at all, do not give it. If they know that some internal or external gift will bring a being certain benefit, whether or not pleasure is certain, or will bring both certain benefit and certain pleasure, they give it.

items.zh: 如是略說菩薩應施不應施已，次當廣辯。

items.title: Section: Detailed Refusals Begin — Never Aiding Coercion or Harm, Whatever the Cost

items.zh: 謂諸菩薩，若有來求共為伴侶，欲作非理逼迫、損害、誑惑於他，便不以身而施於彼，隨所欲為，繫屬於彼、隨順於彼。
items.en: Bodhisattvas, if someone comes seeking companionship in order to unreasonably coerce, harm, or deceive another being, do not give their body to that person to do with as they wish, belonging to them, following their will.

items.zh: 由諸菩薩寧於百反、千反、或百千反，捨自身命施諸眾生，終不隨他教命、稱悅彼情，於諸眾生非理逼迫、損害、誑惑。
items.en: Bodhisattvas would rather give up their own body and life a hundred times, a thousand times, or a hundred thousand times over to benefit beings, than ever follow another's command or gratify their wishes by unreasonably coercing, harming, or deceiving other beings.

items.zh: 若諸菩薩於所行施意樂清淨，見有無量利眾生事正現在前，設有來求自身支節，不應施與。何以故？非彼菩薩於所行施意樂不淨，心生退弱，作是念言：此應可施，此不可施，此應施與，此不應與故。

blocks.text: Fascicle 39 is entirely about the **perfection of giving** (dāna-pāramitā), the first of the six perfections, analysed in nine aspects. Its detail is practical: what to give, when not to give, and how.

"Once bodhisattvas have brought the six perfections to completion, they realise awakening": giving, discipline, patience, diligence, concentration, wisdom. Master Cháng Bǎi: they are practised together, not one at a time.

A verse names them: intrinsic nature, comprehensiveness, difficulty, every gateway, a good person's giving, every kind, fulfilling requests, joy in this life and the next, and purity. Master Cháng Bǎi: the verse is worth memorising.

"Having no attachment to their own body or wealth", bodhisattvas give "whatever should genuinely be given": the intention of non-greed, and the deeds it produces. Not every gift should be given. Master Cháng Bǎi: "much given, little merit" is like a fool donating to sacrifices and drinking.

Internal (one's own body), external (possessions), and both. Giving the body: wholly, "to do with as they wish", or in parts. Venerable Miào Jìng: such giving belongs to the higher stages of the path, not to beginners. External things: for use, or full ownership, "letting go completely".

"Bodhisattvas do not, without discernment, give everything to everyone." If a gift brings "pleasure without benefit", they do not give it; if it brings benefit, they give it, pleasant or not. Master Cháng Bǎi: benefit is the cause, pleasure the result. A practical example from him: before giving, ask the person to recite "Amitābha" once with you, planting a seed.
They never give their body to serve someone who wants "to coerce, harm, or deceive another being". "They would rather give up their own life a hundred thousand times than follow such a command."

quiz.q: How does Master Cháng Bǎi describe the bodhisattva's "training" at this point?
options: practising the six perfections while learning — learning by doing, training as one practices
finish all study first, then practice
study theory now, practice in a later life
quiz.why: The treatise opens with the six perfections. Master Cháng Bǎi: bodhisattvas practice the six perfections while learning — learning by doing, training as they practise. Practice and study are not two separate stages.

quiz.q: What does Master Cháng Bǎi advise students to do with the summarising verse "intrinsic nature, comprehensiveness, difficulty…"?
options: this verse of one and a half stanzas should be memorised
quiz.why: The verse names the nine aspects. Master Cháng Bǎi: this verse of one and a half stanzas should be memorised. Venerable Miào Jìng notes that the verse has six lines and the prose explanation follows.

quiz.q: What does the treatise identify as the substance of "giving in its intrinsic nature"?
options: the volition accompanied by non-greed, and the deeds of body and speech it gives rise to, able to give any blameless object
quiz.why: "The volition accompanied by non-greed, and the deeds of body and speech this volition gives rise to, able to give whatever blameless object is called for." Venerable Miào Jìng: "giving in its intrinsic nature" means the very substance of giving.

quiz.q: Explaining "certainty that giving bears fruit," Master Cháng Bǎi cites four kinds of giving and merit. What is his example of "much given, little merit"?
options: building stupas and temples for the three jewels
a foolish person donating to sacrifices, drinking, and song-and-dance
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: "much given, little merit" is like a foolish person donating to sacrifices, drinking, and song-and-dance — no merit or wisdom comes of it. He adds that the warmth of giving comes from certainty that it bears fruit. Giving stingily with ill will is his third kind, "little given, little merit."

quiz.q: If bodhisattvas give only their own body, what does the treatise call this?
options: mixed giving of inner and outer
giving only what is given from without
giving only what is given from within
quiz.why: "First, what is given from within; second, what is given from without. If bodhisattvas give only their own body, this is called giving only what is given from within."

quiz.q: "Giving the body to that person, to do with as they wish, belonging entirely to them." What level of bodhisattva does Venerable Miào Jìng say can actually do this?
options: not one at the outer ordinary stage; it must be at heat, peak, acceptance, highest mundane — the acceptance stage or above
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: this is not something a bodhisattva at the outer ordinary stage can do; it takes the stages of heat, peak, acceptance, and highest mundane — acceptance or above. Master Cháng Bǎi likewise says an ordinary bodhisattva must be at the acceptance stage or above.

quiz.q: What example does Master Cháng Bǎi give of giving so that the recipient gains genuine benefit?
options: ask whether they can recite "Amitābha" with me once; if so, give, planting a wholesome root in their mind
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: ask whether they can recite "Amitābha" with you once; if they can, give — this plants a wholesome root in the recipient's mind. Venerable Miào Jìng's example is bread: after eating it, the person resolves to stop doing evil and do good.
